play.description: At 41 years old, LeBron James continues to defy Father Time while leading a short-handed Lakers squad missing key contributors. Against a Houston team featuring Kevin Durant's return, the veteran forward attacked the rim with authority and threw down a powerful reverse windmill to energize the home crowd. James orchestrated the Lakers offense with seven assists while contributing 28 points and eight rebounds in a 101-94 victory that put Los Angeles up 2-0 in their Western Conference first-round series.

An unsolvable equation since he set foot in the league two decades ago, LeBron James remains unstoppable with the ball in his hands and downhill momentum. Seizing a gap in the Phoenix Suns defense in the final minute of an early season contest, the Los Angeles Lakers star barrels to the hoop and lays in a critical two points. James racked up 21 points, eight rebounds, nine assists, two steals and a pair of blocks in the October 26, 2023 victory.

On a night he was on fire from downtown, LeBron James still blocked off some time to dazzle the crowd with one of his patented gravity-defying throwdowns. A few months before the 19-time All-Star became the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, James was flying high through the Texas air as he came up with a steal on the defensive end and embarked on a 3-on-1 fast break. The King tossed an alley-oop to Russell Westbrook, who instead of landing the dunk himself lofted the ball in midair back to James for a monster one-handed slam. James scored a game-high 39 points while connecting on 7 of 12 3-pointers to go with 11 rebounds and three assists in a 143-138 Los Angeles Lakers win over the San Antonio Spurs on November 26, 2022.

Never underestimate the offensive tricks LeBron James has learned over the years. The Portland Trail Blazers have their hands full trying to keep up, as the 18-time All-Star fakes a long three-pointer and whips a pass inside to a teammate. James then barrels down the lane like a freight train, re-collecting the ball with a head of steam to throw down a vicious, indefensible dunk. James poured in a game-high 31 points on 12 of 18 shooting — along with seven rebounds, eight assists and six triples — to beat Portland 128-109 on November 30, 2022.

With his Los Angeles Lakers falling behind by double digits in a battle of California, LeBron James decided it was time to do what he’s done thousands of times before: turn the intensity up a few notches. Perfectly synchronizing his sprint down the middle of the floor to catch the Los Angeles Clippers unprepared, the former four-time Most Valuable Player turns to his trusted one-handed tomahawk, setting the groundwork for a 19-point comeback at home. Leading the charge, James burned the Clippers to the tune of 35 points, 12 rebounds, seven assists, four 3-pointers, and two blocks in an overtime triumph on November 1, 2023.

Father Time remains undefeated against most, but LeBron James continues rewriting the aging curve at 41 years old. With the Lakers building an early lead in Houston, Marcus Smart lobs a perfect pass toward the rim as James times his approach. The King elevates and flushes a rim-rocking alley-oop that punctuates another dominant performance. James finished with 30 points on exceptional 92.9% shooting as Los Angeles extended their winning streak to seven.

Running the pick-and-roll with LeBron James sometimes appears so easy that it might as well be a cheat code. The 19-time All-Star shares the wealth at home against the Washington Wizards, bringing the ball across halfcourt before gaining access to the lane courtesy of a helpful screen. James baits the defense into focusing on him, but instead of taking the shot himself he drops off a smooth between-the-legs bounce pass to a cutting Thomas Bryant for a two-handed throwdown. James scored a game-high 33 points while adding seven rebounds and nine assists in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 119-117 victory on December 18, 2022.

Even in his 23rd NBA season, LeBron James continues to turn back the clock with explosive plays that leave defenders helpless. With under a minute left in the third quarter at Smoothie King Center, the Lakers legend jumps the passing lane for a steal and took matters into his own hands. Racing up the court in transition, James elevated through traffic and threw down a timeless windmill dunk that brought the Lakers bench to their feet and pushed their lead to 83-79. The King dominated throughout the January 6, 2026 contest, posting 30 points, 8 rebounds and 8 assists on an efficient 10-of-19 shooting.

In a land affectionately known across the globe for its blockbuster movies and A-list stars, LeBron James used the 2024-25’s season opener to introduce a script that, as he noted, even the greatest screenwriters hadn't yet crafted. Attached closely enough to the term “history” for it to be one of his many nicknames, James, famously renowned for his ability to foresee on-court occurrences before they happen, knew precisely how excellence would arrive on October 22, 2024. Checking in at the scorer’s table during the second period’s four-minute mark — something James had unceremoniously done thousands of times — the Los Angeles Lakers superstar found that this instance would be different, given the player standing directly ahead: his son, Bronny James. Marked through NBA’s record books as the first-ever father-son combination to share the hardwood together, the two immediately got to work. The 20-time All-Star, in particular, made his presence felt through an intuitive, veteran-like backdoor cut, followed by a ferocious, trademark tomahawk flush. Adding to a long, expansive list of unforgettable nights since his October 2003 arrival, James’ impact was found through 16 points, five rebounds, four assists, two blocks, and one 3-pointer in a victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The stylistic clash on November 15, 2024 couldn’t have been more unique, as LeBron James led the purple-and-gold into a battle between last year's In-Season Tournament champion, and one still eyeing its first-ever NBA Cup victory. Knowing the urgency the San Antonio Spurs would inevitably bring, James’ approach in title defense No. 1 boiled down, ironically, to one thing: staying on the offensive. Clinging to a one-point lead in the final half-minute, James, working well-documented wink-wink chemistry alongside his All-NBA big man, ambitiously times an around-the-arc cut to the rim with his teammate’s screen. Powerful in his attack with multiple black-jerseyed Spurs giving aggressive chase, James banks in a game-securing layup, drawing both audibly-stunned confusion and admiration from the Alamo crowd. Busy finding additional ways to enter the NBA’s history books, James’ efforts allowed for a fourth-consecutive triple-double, the first stretch of its kind in his 22-year career. Tying Los Angeles’ franchise record along the way, James’ ultimate contribution concluded as follows: 15 points (on 6-of-12 shooting), 16 rebounds, 12 assists, one steal, and one 3-pointer.

The Los Angeles Lakers are back and thriving in the postseason, a return to prominence guaranteed to invoke memories of the Showtime Era. To that effect, put the ball in LeBron James’ hands in transition, flank him with capable teammates and let him put on a show. James’ underhanded no-look dish to Rui Hachimura in Game 6 of the Western Conference semifinals brought the home crowd to its feet. The 19-time All-Star and four-time champion shot 10 of 14 for a team-high 30 points while also mixing in nine rebounds, nine assists and two steals as James and company eliminated the Golden State Warriors in six games with a 122-101 win on May 12, 2023. It was James’ first 30-point playoff performance since the 2020 NBA Finals, and he and the Lakers will look to extend their postseason run when they take on the top-seeded Denver Nuggets in the Western Conference Finals.

LeBron James has long shined on the biggest and brightest stages. As far as the regular season goes, it doesn’t get much bigger or brighter than overtime in New York City. An All-Star in his 19th consecutive season, the Los Angeles Lakers superstar did his part to keep the New York Knicks at bay when he buried a wide-open 3-pointer to give the Lakers a six-point lead with under two minutes to play in regulation. The Knicks rallied to force overtime, but James’ triple-double effort of 28 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists was too much for New York to overcome as the Lakers left the Big Apple with a 129-123 win on January 31, 2023.

Father Time continues to lose battles against LeBron James, who at age 41 still soars like he's chasing his first championship. James spotted an opening in transition and accelerated past two defenders before launching himself toward the rim, where he hammered home a ferocious running dunk.

Take your pick at an all-time playoff record, and with nearly 300 games under his belt, it’s likely that LeBron James’ name settles atop the leaderboard. Calming in his presence during the Los Angeles Lakers’ must-win Game Two, James introduces the Minnesota Timberwolves to two of the statistics he ranks No. 1 in — points and steals — first through a heady pickpocket of Anthony Edwards’ dribble. Eyeballing open-floor opportunities before Minnesota can react, James gets a 22-year boulder rolling downhill, shouldering through Naz Reid and Nickeil Alexander-Walker for a heavily-contested layup through traffic. James discussed Los Angeles’ need to be physical against the Wolves’ fifth-ranked resistance, and in a series-tying victory, the former four-time NBA champion did just that on April 22, 2025. Enjoying what became the first-ever 20-10-5 statline by a 40-year-old during the NBA’s “second season,” James produced 21 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block, and a 3-pointer across a grueling 40-minute duel.

Match LeBron James and the Golden State Warriors on the floor together, and be prepared for unlimited fireworks. Amped up for a “Rivals Week” duel against his storied rival, the 20-year veteran turned back the clock as only he could. Somehow finding a record he hadn’t broken just yet, the Los Angeles Lakers star pivoted into postseason form early, turning in 36 points, his career’s first-ever 20-rebound game, 12 assists, and a pair of 3-pointers. Fighting off the fatigue of a double overtime slugfest, James summoned the energy needed to guarantee a victory, scoring or assisting on 19 of the Lakers’ 27 points in overtime, fueling a win in one of the 2023-24 season’s most competitive battles.

The list of scenarios opponents hope to avoid when playing the purple-and-gold runs quite long. In losing a race in transition, the Utah Jazz, inevitably, managed to run into two of them at once: the Los Angeles Lakers during In-Season Tournament play, and LeBron James with a head of steam in the open floor. In Year 22, and still a top-of-the-world presence when focused in on a fastbreak opportunity, James breaks into a full sprint, helping Los Angeles exploit a three-on-two advantage before Drew Eubanks can get adjusted. Taking a temporary break from his trademark tomahawk, James pulls a switch-hand lefty jam from his arsenal, propelling the Lakers to both a 19-point lead and eventually, a 7-0 all-time record in NBA Cup contests. Orchestrating an alley-oop connection to his fellow All-NBA teammate just one possession prior, James made aerial attacks a go-to on November 19, 2024, as he compiled a 26-point, 12-assist double-double — ninth-most in NBA history — alongside two rebounds and a 3-pointer.

LeBron James has been around long enough to play against fathers and sons, but make no mistake about it: the King is still operating at peak power. James took Jabari Smith Jr. to school 20 years after playing against Smith’s dad in his NBA debut, using a combination of style and strength to get the best of the 19-year-old rookie on a trip up the court before finishing with a thunderous throwdown. James shot 16 for 26 for 48 points — the 100th 40-point outing of his iconic career — and chipped in eight rebounds, nine assists and five 3-pointers in a 140-132 Los Angeles Lakers victory over the Houston Rockets on January 16, 2023.

Left to walk to the sidelines, lamenting the mistakes that came with blowing a double-digit second half lead in back-to-back games in the 2009 Eastern Conference Finals, the Cleveland Cavaliers considered their plan, with only one second remaining, a stunned crowd, and a two-point deficit. As his All-Star point guard —  and inbounder —  would later tell it, Options A, B, and C were LeBron James. Option D? “Big Game James.” Locked into what would become his career’s highest-scoring series, that meant only one option for the Orlando Magic: defeat. Feigning the idea of an alley-oop with just enough conviction to free himself of Hedo Turkoglu’s glue-tight defense, the 2008-09 Most Valuable Player lives up to the stature, drifting towards the top of the key for a pass. Extraordinarily high in his elevation, James sends a 25-foot triple through the net for a jaw-dropping bucket, drawing all 20,562 in attendance out of their seats in celebration. In what the 24-year-old superstar deemed the “biggest shot” of his career to that point, James followed his 49-point Game One masterpiece with 35 points, four rebounds, five assists, one steal, and one 3-pointer on May 22, 2009, tying the series at a game apiece.

Even at this stage of his legendary career, LeBron James can still turn routine transition opportunities into highlight-reel material. Midway through the second quarter on December 28, 2025, the four-time champion filled the lane perfectly as Luka Dončić pushed the pace. The former Mavericks star found LeBron with a perfectly-timed feed, and the King took flight for a spectacular running reverse dunk that had the Crypto.com Arena crowd on its feet. James finished with 24 points on an ultra-efficient 11-of-13 shooting in the Lakers' 125-101 victory.

One point shy of becoming the NBA’s first-ever to cross the 50,000-point career scoring barrier, LeBron James stepped to March 4, 2025’s stage prepared to do what he often does: break records, and add a bit more on top. Unnoticed from across the floor as teammates work a pick-and-roll that occupies the New Orleans Pelicans’ weakside defenders, James —  poetically receiving a pass from a player he’ll someday pass Los Angeles’ “torch” to —  preps for a catch-and-shoot. Pairing his new, one-of-a-kind longevity statistic with a fitting long-range bomb to match, James buries a triple, prompting the admiration of the already-aware home crowd. The beauty was, James still had three quarters to add to the historic 50,002-point (regular season plus postseason) tally, and the Los Angeles Lakers’ star did just that during a seventh-straight victory. The final box score included a 34-point, eight-rebound, six-assist, one-steal, two-block masterpiece, bolstered by outstanding efficiency overall (10-of-18), from deep (5-of-10), and from the free throw line (nine-of-nine). Along the way, James joined his new, similarly-transcendent teammate in becoming the Lakers’ first-ever duo to produce a 30-point, five-triple game simultaneously.

A straight-line path to the rim in transition, for LeBron James, is often the only requirement needed for the Los Angeles Lakers’ one-of-a-kind superstar to stamp his spot on end-of-night highlight reels. Though, as he welcomed the franchise that first introduced him — in his first game as a 40-year-old, no less — the full-circle moment was equally difficult to miss. Kickstarting his vintage sequence by first offering enough of a defensive presence to encourage Darius Garland’s missed bunny, James springs Los Angeles’ open-floor offense into action, unselfishly skipping a pass ahead before immediately receiving it back. Known to the NBA’s highlight reels as the man of 1,000 tomahawks, James, after recognizing Dean Wade’s wisely-made business decision to retreat, ferociously elevates into another. The Lakers couldn’t fulfill their head coach’s request for “close to perfect basketball” against the NBA’s hottest team, but in December 31, 2024’s clash against the Cleveland Cavaliers, the 22-year veteran starred nonetheless. For James, the final tally included 23 points (on 9-of-17 shooting), alongside a four-rebound, seven-assist, one-block, three-triple complement in 34 minutes.

In dire need of a jolt with their in-city rivals seeking to extend their losing streak, LeBron James reinvigorated the Los Angeles Lakers through a tried-and-true formula: the coast-to-coast fastbreak dunk. Reacting quickly in turning his teammate’s deflection into a steal, the 20-time All-Star turns back the clock, taking the ball the length of the floor before taking flight for a vintage one-handed tomahawk slam over a LA Clippers star. Unbothered by the opposition’s new star power, James proved to be the star of the show in the three-point victory on January 7, 2024, recording 25 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, one steal, and one 3-pointer.

Of all his many accomplishments on a basketball court, LeBron James had never started a postseason game this hot. The 20-year veteran wasted no time in getting to work against the Denver Nuggets in Game 4 of the Western Conference Finals, scoring on an array of layups, fadeaways and 3-pointers as he did everything in his power to stave off a series sweep. James shot 11 for 13 from the field and 4 for 4 behind the arc as he poured in 31 first-half points, his highest-scoring postseason half in a career spanning 282 games. The 19-time All-Star shot 15 of 25 in the game for 40 points while also mixing in 10 rebounds, nine assists, two steals and four treys for the Los Angeles Lakers on May 22, 2023. It was the 29th 40-point playoff game of James’ career — the second most in NBA history.

To make one’s claim as perhaps the greatest, longest-enduring statistical talent in the NBA’s history, it’s only inevitable that at some point, a trademark, career-defining signature move will come about. Over a seven-second span, LeBron James introduced the Memphis Grizzlies to two of them from his toolbox over the last 22 seasons. Plenty capable of soaring with the best of them, even at an advanced age, James commands the highlight reel’s investment, first by punishing Memphis’ disorganized transition defense through a powerful, go-to tomahawk jam. Recognizing Desmond Bane’s desire to offer a quick rebuttal, James — one step behind in his defensive tracking — hustles into the angle needed for a chasedown block, flawlessly sending a two-way message early into December 15, 2024’s game. The first game back was a productive one for the multi-time Most Valuable Player, as he stuffed the box score with 18 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, one steal, two blocks, and three 3-pointers, ultimately steering victory against a familiar foe.

We’ve officially reached the thousands, perhaps quite literally, in terms of the number of statistics one could use to explain the ageless gracefulness of the Los Angeles Lakers’ superstar in Year 22, but for a legend’s sake, here’s one more. The oldest players to make an All-NBA team; a 40-year-old LeBron James, a 39-year-old by the name of LeBron James —  you might’ve heard of him — and a 38-year-old megastar that some refer to as “The King.” Whether he overpowered opponents with still-breathtaking athleticism or conquered them mentally, James did it like few others could, mixing trademark chasedown blocks and tomahawks with clutch buckets and see-everything dimes. James’ 2024-25 season was, in many ways, unlike anything basketball history had ever chronicled, as he guided the third-seeded Lakers’ title pursuit with future Hall of Famers and family members alike. Reinventing himself and remaining elite at what previously worked at once, James’ final averages read as follows: 24.4 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 8.2 assists per game on standout efficiency (51-38-78 percentage splits) across the floor.

20 seasons into a career that leaves him with both accolades and a trophy case capable of stacking up against whole NBA franchises, LeBron James checked his calendar and prepared himself to conquer a stage that he hadn’t before: the newly-designed In-Season Tournament. With just two-and-a-half minutes separating his Los Angeles Lakers from the first-ever In-Season Tournament crown, James maintains his intensity, advancing the ball the length of the floor to a teammate, only to receive it right back with an isolation opportunity. Pairing the tenacious, determined look in his eyes with an early career-like pep in his step, the 20-time All-Star renders Tyrese Haliburton — and the Indiana Pacers’ help defense —  powerless, storming through the lane with a ferocious, double-clutch jam, pushing the Lakers’ lead to 15. Driven by the goal of seeing his younger, less-heralded teammates earn the six-figure bonus associated with winning the tournament, James again rose to a big-stage occasion. Overwhelming a familiar foe once more on December 9, 2023, James lit up the scoreboards for 24 points, 11 rebounds, four assists, and two steals, earning both a win and the Most Valuable Player Award for his efforts throughout.

During the NBA’s recently-released “NBA OGs: Friends & Rivals” interview, LeBron James — with this generation’s two other most influential superstars sitting alongside — was asked about what skill he would take from Stephen Curry, if possible. Opting for a no-brainer pick in shooting ability, it wouldn’t be long before James found his wish coming true. Guaranteed to bring an electric individual performance whenever the Golden State Warriors are scheduled, the Los Angeles Lakers’ future Hall of Famer took his greatness a step further, all the while taking multiple steps backward. Video game-like during a second quarter avalanche, James starts the downpour innocently enough, turning a catch-and-shoot opportunity into a spot-on triple. Seconds later, James, after collecting Draymond Green’s missed bunny, turns the Warriors’ lax defense into a second triple, ballooning the Lakers’ lead to 19. Confident, and officially approaching en fuego-like levels from deep, James tests his range on a 34-footer, stopping at midcourt to complete a three-triples-in-36-seconds sequence with flawless execution. Extraordinary beyond superlative, James concluded February 6, 2025’s win with 42 points (on 14-of-25), alongside a 17-rebound, eight-assist, one-steal, one-block, six-triple complement. History followed closely behind, as James became both NBA history’s youngest and oldest to produce a 40-point performance.

When the Toronto Raptors suggested overtime, LeBron James and the Cleveland Cavaliers laughed all the way to the bank. Following a game-tying triple from rookie O.G. Anunoby with eight seconds remaining in Game 3 of the Eastern Conference semifinals, the King had final say on the outcome. James calmly took the inbound pass from Kevin Love, dribbled the length of the court and whisked past Anunoby on a drive to his left before flicking a one-handed runner off the glass right in front of the Raptors’ bench that sent all of Cleveland into pandemonium. James leapt into Love’s arms to celebrate the improbable as the Cavaliers took a commanding 3-0 series lead after stealing the first two games of the series in Toronto. Cleveland thwarted a furious fourth-quarter Toronto rally behind 38 points, six rebounds, seven assists and three steals from James in the exhilarating 105-103 victory on May 5, 2018. The Cavs won the series two nights later in a Game 4 sweep, giving James a 12-2 record against Toronto the past three postseasons.

Consult the NBA’s all-time history books, and they’ll confirm that there are two things LeBron James has been elite at from the moment he arrived: climbing the leaderboards and climbing the ladder. Camped along the defense’s weak side with the opportunity to deliver an early-game message quickly looming, the 20-year veteran rotates into the paint to challenge the Denver Nuggets’ cut to the rim. Timing his leap through the air perfectly, James wins the high-profile, at-the-rim battle against Jamal Murray, swatting the dunk attempt away with emphasis before capping the moment with a celebratory staredown. Ultimately falling one bucket shy in the two-point defeat, James remained a must-watch during the Game Two thriller on April 22, 2024. Active and productive across the board, the Los Angeles Lakers superstar put together 26 points, eight rebounds, 12 assists, two steals, two blocks, and three 3-pointers.

In the 20th season of his iconic career, it was only fitting that LeBron James’ first-ever 20-20 game got the Los Angeles Lakers one step closer to the semifinals. Trailing the Memphis Grizzlies by two points in the closing seconds of Game 4 of the First Round, James rumbled toward the basket and converted a driving layup in traffic with less than a second to play to send the game to overtime. The seventh-seeded Lakers ultimately took a commanding 3-1 series lead behind James’ 22 points, 20 rebounds and seven assists in the 117-111 triumph on April 24, 2023.

Having watched his superstardom transcend every environment —  from the baggy-clothed, midrange-heavy era to the player empowerment, 3-point revolution, and every chapter in between —  LeBron James has found a blueprint to greatness that knows no limits. As he strolled onto the floor for an Easter Sunday duel, ready to zip full-court dimes and rain triples all over the Brooklyn Nets’ parquet, it turned out his accuracy knew no bounds, either. One well-executed stretch away from pairing one of his career’s greatest shooting exhibitions with a win, the four-time Most Valuable Player gets active, powering through a screen with vigor down the left baseline. Rhythmic in his stepback drift to the far-left corner, James buries his night’s eighth triple, extending the Los Angeles Lakers’ already-commanding lead. The night’s box score anomalies ran long, highlighted by the Lakers’ starters scoring 114 of a possible 116 points, and James’ contributions proved no different. Nearly perfect in needing only 10 attempts to tie his career-high of nine 3-pointers, James was unspeakably efficient. In a perfect complement, the Lakers star also added 40 points (on just 17 shots), seven rebounds, and five assists on March 31, 2024.

LeBron James running the break is a sure sign to get your popcorn ready. The King was off to the races after he scooped up a loose ball on the defensive end and passed off to an in-transition Dennis Schröder, whose eyes lit up when he realized he and James had the Charlotte Hornets’ defense beat on a 2-on-1 fast break. Schröder lobbed an alley-oop to his superstar teammate, who wowed the Charlotte crowd with a high-flying reverse windmill slam. James shot 16 for 26 for a game-high 43 points while mixing in 11 rebounds and six assists in a 121-115 Los Angeles Lakers victory on January 2, 2023. During a season when he became the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, James was named an All-Star for a record-tying 19th time.

The King's passing remains one of his strongest skills. Just before his 39th birthday, LeBron James helped the Lakers take down the Phoenix Suns in a knockout game for the In-Season tournament. James' master class was punctuated by this beautiful one-handed no look pass, threading the defense en route to an easy Taurean Prince finish at the rim. James finished the game with 31 points, 8 boards, 11 assists, and 5 steals as the Lakers took down the Suns on December 5, 2023.

In a season that ultimately became somewhat defined by swaps between the Los Angeles Lakers and Dallas Mavericks, LeBron James used January 7, 2025’s showdown to offer a through-the-air exchange that could only be described as unpleasant. Hardly a week removed from suggesting that he could play at a high level for “another five-to-seven years,” Lake Show’s 40-year-old marvel tests both time and gravity once more, first disconnecting Dallas’ defense through a series of passes. As if deciding to merely handle matters himself after teammates’ attempts go futile, James — cutting through the floor’s middle like a pinball between the two bumpers — springs into an acrobatic, switch-hand throwdown, leaving teammates’ jaws agape for the umpteenth time. James’ early-game poster made for great eye candy on the highlight reel, but the Wild West’s reigning champions used a second-half runaway to leave the scoreboard as a sight for sore eyes for the purple-and-gold. Efficient and extraordinary nevertheless, James tallied 18 points (on 6-of-12 shooting), 10 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, and a triple in 35 minutes.

LeBron James has an innumerable amount of iconic plays across his legendary 20-year career, yet few resonate quite like “The Block.” The Golden State Warriors won a record 73 games during the regular season and held a 3-1 series lead over James’ Cleveland Cavaliers in the NBA Finals, but the league’s all-time leading scorer brought his hometown squad back from the brink. With the deciding Game 7 tied at 89 with under two minutes to play, the King kept it deadlocked as he thwarted a Warriors transition attack by chasing down Andre Iguodala and swatting his driving layup attempt with flawless anticipation. Kyrie Irving’s 3-pointer less than a minute later gave the Cavs the lead for good and James iced the game at the foul line with 10 seconds left to deliver the city its first basketball title in franchise history. Cleveland became the first NBA team to rally from a 3-1 series deficit in the Finals, and James’ third championship ended a 52-year pro sports title drought for the city. The 19-time All-Star posted 27 points, 11 rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and three blocks in the dramatic 93-89 victory on June 19, 2016 to win his third of four Finals MVP awards.

The Decision that captivated the basketball world on July 8, 2010 brought the league's reigning Most Valuable Player to South Beach with championship aspirations burning bright. The two-time MVP arrived carrying unfinished business from Cleveland, joining forces with Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh to form the legendary "Heatles" that would reshape the NBA landscape. James wasted little time establishing his dominance in South Beach, averaging 26.7 points, 7.5 rebounds and 7.0 assists during his inaugural Heat campaign while leading Miami to their first Finals appearance since 2006. What followed transformed Miami from Wade's lone championship franchise into a dynasty: four consecutive Finals appearances and back-to-back titles in 2012 and 2013 that established the Heatles as one of the most dominant teams in NBA history.

Ensured of their respect from the history books after 55-plus win seasons and deep playoff runs in each of the previous three years, the Sacramento Kings wouldn't have found many arguments regarding their status among the NBA’s royalty. Yet, as they stood on the opposite side of what some described to be sports history’s “most anticipated debut,” they — like the rest of the Association —  would learn that the player known as “The King” had arrived for his share of the proverbial crown. Checking every box from Day One on the professional scene, LeBron James, amidst weighted expectations unlike no other, rose to the occasion in both a literal and figurative sense. Be it through a soft, inside-the-arc touch, or a more aggressive, calculated finish at the rim, the Cleveland Cavaliers’ soon-to-be megastar left both the 2.5 million households and the cowbell-bearing ARCO Arena in a collective awe. Victory wouldn't arrive on October 29, 2003, but the James-led Cavaliers left their title-contending opponents with a memorable, competitive battle nonetheless. Previewing a one-of-a-kind career that would eventually offer every atmosphere, award, and highlight type conceivable, James’ debut concluded with 25 points (on 12-of-20 shooting), six rebounds, nine assists, and four steals.

A polarizing, league-changing presence from the moment he first laced his sneakers and stepped onto the hardwood, LeBron James has left an indelible, undisputed mark on nearly every record the NBA’s history books has to offer. Positioned along the top of the key with a chance to become the Association’s first-ever 40,000-point scorer and the arena’s suspense swelling with his every dribble, the 20-time All-Star makes his move, muscling past Michael Porter Jr.’s defensive resistance with a spin move into the paint before softly arcing a left-handed finish off the glass. Already woven into the fabric of league history, James took time to celebrate his milestone before getting back to business in the loss to the Denver Nuggets on March 2, 2024. Valiant in his efforts, the Los Angeles Lakers superstar concluded the unforgettable night with 26 points, four rebounds, nine assists, three steals, and a pair of 3-pointers.

Karl Malone's name had sat atop the record books for 22 years, but the longest career in NBA history has a way of rewriting them. Early in the first quarter against the Dallas Mavericks on February 12, 2026, LeBron James fires a catch-and-shoot triple over PJ Washington, swish, then moments later, rises up on an early shot clock 35-footer over Washington again, and drains it clean at the 8:50 mark. Back-to-back threes in 22 seconds, in the 23rd season of a career that refuses to wind down. By night's end, James had become the oldest player in NBA history to record a triple-double at 41 years and 44 days old, surpassing Malone's mark by nearly a year, while also extending his record for the longest streak of double-digit assist games by any player 40 or older. His 123rd career triple-double, fifth all-time, arrived in a 124-104 victory as he finished with 28 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists.

Come for four-time NBA Champion LeBron James casually burying one of the most efficient shots in basketball, stay for the next-level celebration. James sinks the corner triple against the Houston Rockets on January 12, 2021 then turns to face the Los Angeles Lakers bench before the ball even finds the net.

When LeBron James hits the open court, the world stops and watches. In a December 23, 2005 matchup against the Indiana Pacers, the third-year Cleveland Cavaliers forward chases down a stolen ball, crosses halfcourt all alone and explodes for a two-handed, windmill reverse slam. James logged 14 points, eight rebounds and nine assists in the win.
Los Angeles Lakers superstar LeBron James drives the lane and throws down a wicked one-handed slam against Western Conference rivals the Sacramento Kings on November 15, 2019.

After 18 years of watching him make it look easy, you’d think it would get old watching LeBron James take off with an open lane to the basket. James catches an outlet pass from Nikola Jokić then hovers through the paint for a double-clutch reverse slam in the NBA All-Star Game on March 7, 2021.

The double-clutch hammer! LeBron James of the Los Angeles Lakers catches a beautiful bounce pass on his way to the rim for a massive two-handed slam against the Miami Heat during fourth quarter action of Game 1 of the NBA Finals on September 30, 2020.

That’s my quarterback! LeBron James sizes up a defensive rebound as it caroms off the rim then immediately throws a perfect spiral down the court to a streaking Kentavious Caldwell-Pope on January 10, 2021. James put up 18 points, seven rebounds and seven assists in the Los Angeles Lakers’ win over the Houston Rockets.
Hang time with The King! Los Angeles Lakers superstar LeBron James throws down the showtime two-handed reverse windmill slam against Western Conference foes the Houston Rockets on February 6, 2020.

LeBron James is a load for any transition defense to handle. Give him two teammates in a 3-on-2, and it’s game over. After generating a stop on defense, the Los Angeles Lakers star sprints down the court while the ball advances up the floor, then relays a pass from Kent Bazemore over his shoulder to Anthony Davis for a fastbreak jam. James started Year 19 off on a hot note, with 34 points, 11 rebounds, five assists, a steal and a block against the Golden State Warriors on October 19, 2021.

Throughout his illustrious 19-year career, Los Angeles Lakers superstar LeBron James has never shied away from a clutch moment, whether he’s making a play for himself or one of his teammates. He takes the Lakers’ destiny into his own hands with a confident, sidestep triple from way downtown followed by his signature “Silencer” celebration to quiet the crowd late in the fourth quarter. James’ huge shot was a part of a monster 39-point effort in a 124-116 overtime win over the Indiana Pacers on November 24, 2021.

No matter the age, situation, or defensive coverage, Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James makes the game of basketball look effortless. James showcases his world-class athleticism by sneaking backdoor on a cut, turning teammate Malik Monk’s lob into a reverse alley-oop slam to send the crowd into a frenzy. James racked up a 30-point, 12-rebound, five-assist performance on January 19, 2022.

No vision, no problem. With his Los Angeles Lakers knotted against the Golden State Warriors in the final minute of a Western Conference play-in game, LeBron James pulls up from way beyond the three-point line for what would go on to be the game-winning bucket. James, unable to see straight as a result of contact on a previous play, finished with a triple-double in addition to the No. 7 seed in the May 19, 2021 contest.

The sheer power LeBron James can generate downhill toward the bucket has stifled defenses for nearly two decades. The Los Angeles Lakers forward pushes the ball up the floor in the final seconds of a quarter before unleashing a thundering assault on the rim that no mere mortal would possibly want a part of. The 36-year-old finished with 22 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists in the February 14, 2021 showdown against the Denver Nuggets.
In hot pursuit! Los Angeles Lakers superstar LeBron James chases down a driving Kyle Lowry and executes the picture-perfect, from-behind block against the Toronto Raptors on August 1, 2020.

Get up, Mr. James! Superstar LeBron James of the Los Angeles Lakers gets way up for a thunderous alley-oop slam in Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals against the Denver Nuggets on September 18, 2020.

Showing off the range! In his 15th appearance in a Christmas Day game, Los Angeles Lakers superstar LeBron James shakes off  Luka Dončić on defense and drops the pretty step back three pointer against the Dallas Mavericks on December 25, 2020. James finished the game with 20 points, moving him past NBA icon Oscar Robertson for second place on the all-time Christmas Day scoring list with 383 total points.

On the same night he was named on the NBA’s 75th Anniversary Team, Los Angeles Lakers superstar LeBron James found himself with the perfect opportunity to ice the game for his team with one final shot. James takes his time on the mismatch and knocks down a textbook fadeaway jumper over two defenders for the win. It was a storybook ending for Team LeBron in his adopted hometown of Cleveland, Ohio. James finished with 24 points, eight assists, six rebounds and the game-winning J to defeat Team Durant and move to 5-0 as an All-Star captain on February 20, 2022.

The LeBron James-Dwyane Wade connection is one of the most devastating duos you’ll ever see in transition. LeBron finds Wade streaking on the break, sprints down court and slams home a return feed from Wade, off the glass, with an incredible left-handed flush. LeBron finished with 19 points, eight boards and four dimes in Miami’s 101-95 win over the Los Angeles Lakers on December 25, 2013.

It’ll take a lot more than friendship and a shared 2016 title to spare Kevin Love the destructive wrath of LeBron James at full throttle. Well-positioned to capitalize on a gap in the Cleveland Cavaliers defense, the 37-year-old Los Angeles Lakers forward drives straight to the paint and takes off skyward for a thundering flush over his former teammate. James dropped 38 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists in the March 21, 2022 victory.

With authority! Los Angeles Lakers superstar LeBron James explodes to the rim for a massive slam over the defense of the Miami Heat late in the third quarter of Game 6 of the NBA Finals on October 11, 2020. James notched a stellar triple double in Game 6 with 28 points, 14 rebounds, and 10 assists on the way to winning his fourth career championship and number 17 for the Los Angeles Lakers franchise.
